T1595.name: Active Scanning
T1595.description: Adversaries may execute active scanning probes to gather information targeted at networks, systems, or services before launching an infiltration.

T1110.name: Brute Force
T1110.description: Adversaries may use brute force techniques to guess credentials for accounts across services such as SSH, RDP, or SMB.

T1210.name: Exploitation of Remote Services
T1210.description: Adversaries may exploit vulnerable remote services (such as SMB port 445 or RPC endpoints) to gain unauthorized access or move laterally.

T1071.name: Application Layer Protocol
T1071.description: Adversaries may communicate using application layer protocols (such as HTTP/HTTPS or DNS) to cloak command and control traffic within normal web activity.

T1041.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
T1041.description: Adversaries may pilfer data by copying it over their existing command and control channel to an external server.

T1078.name: Valid Accounts
T1078.description: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of existing accounts as a means of gaining initial access, persistence, privilege escalation, or defense evasion.
